settings.title: Flat-Fee Nil T2 Filing for Dormant IT Consulting Corporations

settings.editor:
An IT corporation between contracts still files, with a closed statement of work behind it, a workstation still on the books, and a business number that stays open until somebody closes it. We file bench years at $300.00 plus HST per tax year, so the entity is ready when the next contract needs it.

Whether you incorporated because a client or an agency required it, moved to agency payroll when the project closed, took ordinary employment, or are waiting for the next statement of work, we read the corporate card before treating a year as nil, keep equipment on Schedule 8 while it is owned, and sign one T183CORP per year online. settings.html:
The year is nil

  • No statement of work, milestone or change request was billed
  • No cloud, hosting, domain or certificate charge hit the corporation
  • No equipment or licence was bought, sold or written off by it
  • No referral, affiliate or vendor commission was received
  • It paid no salary, dividend or management fee to anyone

The year is not nil

  • A closing milestone or holdback on an old contract was billed
  • A compute, hosting or domain account charged the corporate card
  • A workstation, server or device was sold, traded or written off
  • A vendor or partner programme paid a commission or a rebate
  • The corporation reimbursed the owner for anything at all

Due either way

  • A T2 for every tax year the corporation exists
  • One signed T183CORP covering each of those years
  • An equipment list, because what is on the books decides Schedule 8
  • The business number, which stays open until it is closed
  • A clean filing record, which agencies ask for at onboarding

Dormant IT consulting corporations are filed the same way wherever the registered office sits, because the return is prepared and transmitted electronically from end to end. There is nothing to print, nothing to post and nothing to sign in person.

Where the corporation was incorporated changes the registry, not the return. An Ontario corporation answers to the Ontario Business Registry, and corporations in British Columbia, Alberta, Quebec and Saskatchewan each answer to their own. The T2 itself is federal and identical in all of them. Within Ontario, a corporation registered in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton or Ottawa is filed on the same terms and at the same price as one anywhere else in the country.

Two provinces add a return the federal T2 does not cover. A Quebec corporation also files the CO-17 and an Alberta corporation also files the AT1. Both are separate provincial returns, and neither is included in the $300.00 plus HST fee.
